pm_exper_user_1766_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.question: How can I keep my anxiety under control when I have to speak in front of a large audience?
pm_exper_user_1766_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) Before speaking in front of a large audience, focus on the main ideas you want to communicate and imagine having a conversation with a friendly group rather than performing. Practicing your talk with supportive friends or colleagues can also help you feel more relaxed when the moment arrives.
(b) When preparing to speak at an important environmental forum, ground yourself by picturing it as a dialogue with collaborators who care about your insights on Florida’s urban ecosystems. Practice in a space or with people who resemble your eventual audience so you can step into the room with that sense of recognition and ease.
(c) Ahead of your keynote at a major environmental conference, anchor yourself in the central story you want to tell about Florida’s shifting coastal ecology, and imagine it as a shared conversation with allies. You might also draw on the composure you find birdwatching in local wetlands to carry that same steady focus into your presentation.
(d) Before stepping onto the stage at a high-profile environmental conference, take a moment to center yourself by focusing on the key takeaway you want to share about Florida’s urban ecological history. Remind yourself that you’re speaking to peers who value your expertise, and rehearse with colleagues who can emulate the kinds of policymakers and scientists you’ll face so the setting feels familiar.

One approach is to create a gentle transition ritual between work and personal time — something sensory and grounding. Since you mentioned chopping basil, you could make the act of cooking a mindful experience: notice the colors, scents, and textures, and give yourself permission to focus only on the meal in front of you. Pair it with a small, consistent boundary — like closing your laptop and physically moving to a different space before you cook. Over time, your mind will start to recognize these cues as a sign to shift gears. You might also experiment with planning an engaging personal activity right after work hours so your brain reorients toward something completely different from research.
